answer.rationale: Memory 57 is the most direct evidence because it reports qualified revenue and no measurable retention harm, though it is limited to established customers and omits longer-term economics. Memory 44 strongly supports qualified pipeline creation for enterprise prospects, but omits closed-won revenue, retention, and unit economics. Memories 31 and 86 show durable/early activation and adoption improvements, useful leading indicators but not direct evidence of qualified revenue or long-term retention. Memory 73 shows acquisition and revenue lift in the relevant price-sensitive SMB segment, but promotional pricing can impair durability and it omits retention, discount depth, margin, and customer quality. Memory 91 reports only week-one engagement and first meaningful action, with no evidence of revenue, qualification, retention, or durability.
